Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the AetherCloud Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star one on your telephone keypad followed by your name and company. There will be an opportunity to ask a follow-up question if time permits. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing AetherCloud's results for the Q3 FY2024. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. AetherCloud had a strong Q3, driven by continued growth in our cloud platform and increasing adoption of our AI-powered services.

During the quarter, we focused on four key areas:
1. Expanding our global infrastructure.
2. Enhancing our platform security.
3. Driving innovation in AI and machine learning.
4. Strengthening our partnerships.

Let me elaborate on our investments in security infrastructure and personnel, one of our top priorities in this hyperscaler landscape where AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud handle multi-trillion-dollar workloads. Security is our foundational moat protecting our $115 billion ARR platform. Ransomware incidents are up 62% year-over-year according to the Verizon DBIR, and with 92% of enterprises adopting multi-cloud per Flexera's 2023 State of the Cloud Report, breaches can spread rapidly. Our forward-thinking approach has boosted net revenue retention by 15% year-over-year to 128%, as customers like Fortune 500 banks and healthcare providers shift workloads to us for better threat protection.

In FY2024 so far, we've committed $850 million to security, up 28% from $665 million in FY2023, accounting for 12% of total OpEx and 22% of our $3.9 billion CapEx. That's risen from 9% of OpEx two years back, aligning with the push to zero-trust amid state-sponsored risks. Of that, $520 million, or 61%, funded infrastructure, the rest personnel. Results include mean time to detect threats down to 14 minutes from 28, and mean time to respond under two hours, surpassing Ponemon benchmarks.

On infrastructure, we've poured resources into cloud-native defenses. We spent $250 million on confidential computing and hardware security modules across our 45 global edge data centers, using Intel SGX and AMD SEV-SNP for tenant isolation in sensitive AI/ML workloads. This tackles the 40% uptick in supply-chain attacks like SolarWinds, with FIPS 140-3 certification drawing regulated sectors—confidential compute revenue up 180% to $450 million.

Another $150 million went to AI/ML-driven SecOps via our Nebula Shield platform, with generative AI spotting anomalies at 98.7% accuracy across 10 petabytes of daily Kubernetes telemetry. False positives dropped 65% versus legacy SIEMs like Splunk. Integrations with CrowdStrike Falcon and Palo Alto Prisma Cloud handle 500,000+ DDoS events daily, up 35% amid 5.6 Tbps volumetric peaks.

We allocated $120 million to quantum-resistant cryptography, migrating 70% of key management to Kyber and Dilithium ahead of NIST standards, guarding against harvest-now-decrypt-later risks as quantum advances from IBM and Google loom.

Regionally, EMEA got $180 million, or 35% of security CapEx, for Schrems II and GDPR via EU sovereign zones—EMEA revenue up 42% versus AWS's 30%. APAC's $140 million addressed data sovereignty in Tokyo and Singapore with homomorphic encryption for Japan's My Number Act, grabbing 25% financial services share over Alibaba Cloud. Americas invested $200 million in HIPAA and CMMC Level 2 for DoD FedRAMP High, securing 12 contracts over Azure Government.

Personnel investments hit $330 million, up 32%, growing our security team to 3,200 FTEs—28% headcount rise, 8% of our 40,000 workforce. That's 1,200 engineers with CISSP, CCSP, GCIH certs, averaging 4.2 years tenure. Our $50 million CloudSec Academy trains 800 internals and 200 externals yearly in Rust secure coding and eBPF. Pay is 15% above Bay Area medians amid ISC2's 300,000 vacancy gap. Our 1:8 security-to-engineer ratio beats Azure's 1:12.

With 65% multi-cloud customers per our surveys, up from 52%, we're the secure interconnect via StratoLink with Istio/Linkerd service mesh. Secure Workload Platform cross-sell hit 72%, adding $2.1 billion ARR. GCP lags on confidential computing; our 99.9995% uptime SLA cuts churn 40% below averages.

For FY2025, $1.05 billion slated for security, up 23%, with 40% on GenAI red-teaming and 25% edge for 5G/IoT. ROI is 22x via avoided breaches—our sims cost $1.2 million vs. IBM's $4.45 million benchmark. This is strategic insurance.

Now I'll turn the call over to Jordan to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong financial performance in the Q3. Revenue grew by 21% year-over-year to $28.7 billion. Our gross margin was 75.2%, and our operating margin was 32.4%.

I'm thrilled to highlight our overall financial performance, showcasing the resilience of our IaaS, PaaS, and AI/ML workloads against a dynamic macro backdrop, much like peers AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. Total revenue hit $28.7 billion, up 21% YoY and 7% QoQ—our 15th straight 20%+ quarter, beating Gartner's 17% cloud market growth. ARR topped $115 billion, +23% YoY, with $4.2 billion net new ACV—record expansions and logos. RPO at $185 billion, +28% YoY; current RPO $95 billion.

By category: Compute and networking $12.4 billion, +24%, led by AetherGraviton4 ARM instances with 30% better price-perf than x86, like AWS Graviton/Azure Cobalt, ramping for Meta/OpenAI. Storage/databases $8.1 billion, +19%, with 150 EB monthly AetherStore S3 and 35% Aurora growth from Oracle migrations. AI/ML/analytics $4.2 billion, +45%, 15% of revenue—Bedrock with NVIDIA H100 via DGX Cloud took 40% GenAI share per IDC, wins in bank fraud LLMs. Other services $4.0 billion, +18%, edge/SaaS.

Customer adds: 1,200 net new to 85,000 total; $1M+ ARR customers 4,200, +32%; NRR 118%, dollar expansion >110%. Churn <1% large enterprise via Sovereign Cloud.

Profitability: GAAP gross margin +210bps to 75.2% on 92% DC utilization (from 88%), $2.5 billion supply chain savings from cooling/renewables. Non-GAAP op margin 32.4%, +400bps; OpEx +15% to $9.1 billion—$1.8B sales/marketing for AI GTM, $2.2B R&D on quantum encryption/zero-ETCD.

Net income $8.9 billion, $0.84 EPS, +8% beat. Op cash $15.2 billion, FCF $11.4 billion +25%, 40% revenue. Cash $85 billion; $4B buybacks, $10B DC capex. Capex $12.3 billion (43% revenue), to 35-38% FY2025.

Regions: Americas (65%) $18.7B +22%, FedRAMP AI deals. EMEA (20%) $5.7B +19%, EU certs. APAC (15%) $4.3B +25%, India/Japan.

$20B FY2025 capex for 50+ edge zones/2M GPU eq., 30%+ AI growth. AetherOutposts cut latency 60% for IoT/AV; 100% renewables by 2026 at 85% now. Neutral marketplace 500+ ISVs.

This flywheel—innovation to adoption to reinvestment—sets us up. Q4 guide $29.5-30.0B revenue (20-22% YoY), op income $9.8-10.0B; FY2024 $114-115B, FY2025 ARR +25%+.

Now, I'll hand it back to Alex for further comments.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Jordan. We are particularly excited about the momentum we are seeing with AetherBedrock, which is driving significant AI revenue growth for our customers.

Looking ahead, let me address the expected impact of macroeconomic factors on our business through FY2025. As a hyperscaler competing with AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud at the nexus of digital transformation, AI, and economic cycles, our 22% Q3 growth from 35% AI surge keeps us vigilant.

Elevated rates at 4.5-5% pressure capex, deferring on-prem 20-30% like Microsoft's Azure moderation. Our FY25 capex $18-20B (25% revenue) shifts to liquid-cooled H100/H200 racks, yielding 2% FCF margin to 28%, but 100-150bps gross compression from $15B debt at SOFR+125bps. Countering with Capex-as-a-Service via Goldman Sachs, $2.5B commitments.

Global GDP at 2.7% IMF drags growth 2-3pp to 18-22% from 23-27%; RPO slowed to 28%. NA 25% on AI (GenAI 42% capacity); EMEA 12-15% on regs/AI Act, PUE 1.35 countered by GovCloud 15% Germany share; APAC 30%+ India/Japan subsidies, FX hedge 80%.

AI tailwinds +5pp: Gartner $679B cloud, 45% AI; AI Foundry with Claude/Llama 55% attachment, ARR +31%, FY25 $8B AI (30% revenue). Energy +15% YTD 50bps hit; $1.2B renewables 2.5GW PUE<1.2, 10-15% Green AI premium.

Geopol/supply: 10-15% ASIC risk diversified TSMC/Samsung; inflation 3-5% servers, $300M exposure.

Confident $75-78B FY25 revenue (+20%), op margins +100bps to 32%, EPS $4.85-5.05. Playbook: AI Inference Optimizer Q1 TCO -40%; $500M ARM savings; 75% RPO multi-year, NRR 118%. AI pulls through macro pause.

We continue to invest in research and development to stay ahead of the curve in the rapidly evolving cloud landscape. Our commitment to innovation is reflected in our recent advancements in AI/ML services.

Central to this is our energy efficiency and sustainability initiatives, key to long-term value. As second-largest hyperscaler post-AWS, $28B TTM revenue, 45% IaaS growth, customers in finance/healthcare/AI demand ESG alignment amid EU CBAM/California SB253.

Q3 fleet PUE 1.12 (from 1.18), vs. 1.5 industry; 15% less energy/workload hour, 2.8 TWh saved (~250k homes). Renewables 92% (from 78%), 100% by 2026; Scope 1/2 emissions -28% to 1.2M MT CO2e, Scope 3 reporting.

Financials: Energy 12% DC opex -18% QoQ %revenue, +120bps to 32% margin; $450M FY25 savings.

Hardware: Graviton-A3 65% capacity (from 45%), 40% eff/TOPS AI inference; 3rd-gen immersion cooling 12 sites, -35% cooling, PUE 1.05 Gaudi3.

Software: Optimizer RL on 10PB cuts idle 22% AI jobs +75%; green scheduling Kubernetes NKS, 15-20% bank TCO cuts.

Regions: NA 24 DCs 55% cap, 98% renewables 4.2GW PPAs, sub-1.1 PUE edge 5G. Europe 25% cap PUE 1.10 88% hydro, $200M batteries Ireland/NL. APAC +35% cap 75% renewables RECs Singapore MoU, Sydney/Tokyo 1.15 3nm, hypochlorous cooling WUE<0.2.

Water positive 2030: 1.5B liters reused Q3.

Moat: Green tier 28% new AI, 5% premium; $1.2B ESG finance -50bps; NVIDIA Hopper co-dev. 15% sustainable AI share Synergy.

$3.5B next 3yrs: $1.8B PPAs/nuclear SMR; $900M cooling/silicon; $800M AI R&D quantum opt. 2027 net-zero ops, 50% Scope 3.

This drives FY2024 48-50% growth, 34% margins.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question, please press star one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith:
Thanks for taking my question. Alex, great details on security investments—impressive MTTD improvements. Can you talk more about how these are influencing competitive positioning in multi-cloud deals?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Ben. Absolutely, our security investments are a key differentiator. With StratoLink as the secure fabric, we're seeing 72% penetration of the Secure Workload Platform, driving that $2.1 billion incremental ARR. Customers running hybrid/multi-cloud—and that's now 65% of our base—are choosing us as the trusted layer, leading to lower churn and higher NRR. It's putting pressure on competitors, and we're gaining share in regulated verticals.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Hi, thanks. Jordan, on the financials, your capex guide is moderating—how does that interplay with AI demand ramp?

Jordan Lee:
Great question, Lisa. We're balancing hyperscale AI needs with efficiency. Capex at 35-38% FY2025 supports 2 million GPU-equivalent capacity, but higher utilization and Graviton efficiencies let us optimize. FCF remains robust at 40% of revenue, funding reinvestment without dilution.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel:
Thanks. Dr. Vasquez, on the AI/ML side, how are sustainability initiatives integrating with Bedrock for customer AI workloads?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Raj. Our green scheduling in NKS prioritizes low-carbon zones for Bedrock jobs, delivering 15-20% TCO reductions. With PUE 1.12 and Graviton-A3, customers hit ESG goals while scaling GenAI—early adopters like banks are locking in multi-year commitments.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Gonzalez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Maria Gonzalez:
Hi everyone. Alex, macro headwinds seem persistent—any color on sales cycle impacts in EMEA?

Alex Rivera:
Sure, Maria. EMEA growth tempered to 19% on regs and energy, but sovereign offerings captured 15% Germany share. Sales cycles elongated 10-15% non-AI, but AI offsets with 55% attachment. Overall, NRR holds at 118%, and we're guiding through the pause with AI strength.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions and your continued support. We are confident in our ability to continue to deliver strong results and create long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
